justification: A has a clear, dedicated cover page and bold numbered headings with a serif body, so sections are easy to tell apart (A2, A3). B's light-weight headings with a rule above each are weaker, and its heading 'Creating an Invoice' is stranded at the bottom of B1, away from its code block on B2. B's dark title band is attractive, but its tighter layout and thin headings give less hierarchy. A's code block splits across pages (A2 to A3), which counts against it.

A pairs a serif title and headings with teal rules between sections, which gives an elegant, consistent look and clear section breaks (A1, A2). A's title fits on one line in the dark band. B's title wraps to two lines, and its numbered sans headings mix with the serif body, which is less cohesive. B's running header on page 2 adds a little clutter. The tables and charts are nearly identical in both. B's stronger bold headings scan well, but A feels more refined overall.

B has a full dark cover, thin gold rules and a consistent serif running footer. Its pages feel cohesive and body text is comfortable (B2-B4). A's red band is bold and its sans headings are clearer, but headings hang in the left margin while body text is indented, which looks awkward. A also has a large empty gap on page 1 and a duplicated 'References' heading on A3. B's headings are light and weaker in hierarchy, and B has the same duplicate 'References' and a mostly empty cover and page 2. Overall B is calmer and more polished.

A keeps the paragraph that follows the chart on page 1, so the argument stays together, and its running header band gives page 2 a clear identity. B orphans the closing sentence of 'The problem' at the top of page 2 under a thin rule, and its chart ends in a gap at the bottom of page 1. B's serif text is elegant and its title is on one line, but its page flow is weaker. Both pages 2 leave a large empty space, and the tables are similar.

A uses bold sans numbered headings with clear section and subsection levels, a running header, and fills pages 2 and 3 evenly. B has light, weak headings with repeated heavy rules above each section, which makes the rhythm heavy and the hierarchy flatter. B also splits content across four pages, leaving large empty areas (B2, B4) and a sparse last page. The tables are similar in both. A's hyphenation in justified text is a minor flaw.

A opens with a green title band and runs straight into content. Its callout sits beside the illustration, and its header and footer bands give consistent page framing (A1, A2). B spends a full page on a mostly empty dark cover. B3 is dominated by a stranded illustration with a large blank area at left, and B4 leaves the lower half empty. Both have the same ragged ending on the budget page. B's serif type is elegant, and its callout over the image is nice. A's text-and-image pairing on page 2 also leaves a gap, but A is tighter overall.

A's bold sans headings stand out clearly against the serif body, which gives a stronger hierarchy (A1, A2). B's light serif headings are weaker and blend into the body text (B1, B2). B has a more cohesive palette, with a burgundy chart matching its band and a table with burgundy rules, and its single-line title fits the band. A's black bars clash slightly with the burgundy band, and its indented body text beside outdented headings looks a little odd. A's heading hierarchy still makes the document easier to scan and gives it more presence. Both end page 2 with a large empty space.

B has a compact 3-page flow with a colored title band, consistent running header and footer bands, and tidy sans-serif text and tables. A spends a full page on a mostly empty dark cover and leaves A5 nearly blank with only a short changelog. A's oversized Note callout is out of proportion with the body text, and its code lines wrap awkwardly (A3). B's Note is small and subdued, but its heading hierarchy is a bit flat. B also has a stray orphan sentence at the top of B3.

A uses an elegant serif and a full-bleed cover with a restrained accent line (A1). Its body text is airy and well spaced, and the overlay callout sits on the image (A2). The budget table is clean (A4). B uses a sans-serif with a more generic look. Its heavy footer and header bands are strong but add weight, and the hyphenated 'ar-chitect' in the justified text hurts readability (B3). B's page 2 opens with a text fragment beside the image, which leaves a large empty gap on the left. A also has some loose layout, with a large empty gap beside the image on A3, but it holds together slightly better.

A keeps a consistent left edge, with headings and body text aligned. Its split pull-quote and image panel on A1 is cleaner. Its header and footer bands on A2 and A3 frame the pages, and its table on A3 is bolder with a clear emphasised column. B indents body text away from its headings, so the margins look uneven. B's quote box sits awkwardly over the image on B1, and its body text size changes between paragraphs. B's pages lack header and footer bands.

B has a full-bleed cover, a consistent running header band, a single serif family and an orderly flow. Its pages are cleaner and its footers consistent. A's page 2 is awkward: a justified paragraph with wide gaps sits beside an image, leaving a large void beneath it. A also mixes a sans heading face with a serif body, and its heading indentation is inconsistent. B's image sits alone on page 3 with a big empty left area, which is a weakness, but the page is still tidier overall. The tables are similar, and B's is slightly better spaced.

A opens with a strong navy title band and lets the content start on page 1, with thin rules between sections that give a clear rhythm. B spends a whole page on a sparse cover, and its code block splits across pages 2 and 3, leaving a dangling fragment at the top of B3. B's numbered headings and serif body are pleasant, but its tables wrap awkwardly, as in the error table on B3. A's JSON block also sits on one page (A2) with its field table, and A's tables are tidier. A's body text on A1 and A3 is justified with some wide gaps, a minor flaw.

B uses solid navy section bands and a running header, so sections are easy to find (B2, B3). Its sans-serif is clean and the bands give a consistent rhythm. A is elegant and airy with thin rules and a serif face. Its headings are light and weak, and its section breaks are subtle, so the hierarchy is flatter (A2, A3). B has some hyphenation breaks ("segmenta-tion", "Me-ridian") and justified text with uneven spacing. Both leave page 4 mostly empty, and both have similar tables. B is more scannable and more finished overall.

A has an elegant serif and a refined title page, but its page 2 puts a dark overlay box on the image, which cuts into the picture, and the image on page 3 floats alone at the top right with a large empty area on its left. Its orange rules and body text sizes are consistent. B has a strong cover that uses the illustration, numbered bold sans headings that read clearly, and a full-width green header and footer band that give navigation (B2, B3). Its page 2 callout is split cleanly between the green panel and the image. Both designs leave large empty areas at the bottom of the pages and an orphaned image on page 3. B's hyphenation ("eco-logist") and justified spacing are minor flaws. Overall B is a more structured and more legible document.

B has a full-bleed cover, consistent running header and footer bands, numbered headings, and a clean callout that sits flush with its image (B2). Its body text is a uniform size and its page structure is consistent. A packs the title banner onto the first page, with a dark callout box overlapping the image. A's body text switches size mid-section (A1), and a large empty gap sits beside the paragraph on A2 next to a floating image. A's table is as good as B's, but both leave blank space on the last page.

A's dark navy cover (A1) with a serif title and a navy rule at the top of each inner page (A2-A5) feels more polished and cohesive. Its serif headings and the large serif Note callout (A2) sit well with the body text. B's bold sans headings (B2) are clear, but the margins are inconsistent: headings and rules hang to the left of the indented body text and the code blocks. The blue sans Note in B2 looks less integrated. B's running footer labels are useful, and its tables are comparable to A's. B's cover is plain white. A's overall alignment is tidier.

A has bold numbered sans headings that are easy to scan, running header and footer bands, and a callout note styled as an aside (A2). B uses light, small headings, each preceded by a heavy rule, which weakens hierarchy. B also sets the Note as oversized body text that competes with the headings (B2) and leaves the last page nearly empty (B5). A's tables are compact and well aligned (A3, A4). B's dark cover is striking, but its title sits low and the cover is otherwise a flat dark page.

A fits the content onto three pages with serif body text and numbered headings, so it reads as continuous. Its content pages (A2, A3) are well filled and the tables are clean. B uses heavy navy heading bands that are repetitive. They break up the flow and add visual weight. B also leaves large empty areas on B2, where Phase 2 is pushed to the next page, and on B4, which holds only three list items. The bands do give B strong section markers, but the overall pacing is worse.

A has a refined serif type system and a dark cover with a gold accent rule (A1). Its body text has comfortable leading and clear heading steps (A2-A4), and the tables and chart are clean. B is tidy, but its body text is tight under the headings, its header band is heavy, and its cover is merged with the abstract page (B1). B also shows a duplicated 'References' heading in two styles (B3), which A has too (A4), so that flaw does not separate them. A feels more polished, though it uses more pages and leaves large gaps on A2.

A aligns headings and body on one left margin, and its numbered headings are clear. Its burgundy chart bars match the title band. A also has a running header and a 'Page 2 of 2' footer. B indents the body while its headings hang in the margin, which makes the layout look uneven. B's rules above every heading add clutter, and its near-black chart bars clash with the burgundy band. B's tables are similar to A's.

A has a restrained navy and gold palette, a dedicated cover page (A1), and consistent serif section headings with gold rules (A2-A4). The text column is aligned cleanly. B's headings hang out to the left of an indented body, so the left edge looks misaligned (B1-B3). Its coral banner is loud, and the cover is crammed onto the first content page. Both designs repeat 'References' as a duplicate heading, and both leave gaps at page bottoms. A is more polished and cohesive overall.

A pairs a bold geometric sans for headings with a serif body, so the headings are stronger, but its layout is misaligned: headings sit flush left while body is indented, and the rules run wider than the text. Page 2 ends with a large blank area and page 4 holds only Next Steps. B has a consistent left edge, rules matching the text width, a coherent serif family, and cleaner tables. It also splits sections more sensibly, keeping Why Harbor & Pine with Next Steps. A's hyphenation in body text (seg-mentation, pro-gramme) hurts readability. B's thin light headings are weaker, but the page is more orderly overall.

B has a cover page, running headers and footers, a boxed abstract, a navy-coloured chart with a clear title, and tidy tables. Its flaws are a duplicated 'References' heading (6 References plus References) and a cramped abstract label layout. A also duplicates 'References', and its black chart is plain with a caption below. Its table caption sits tight against the preceding paragraph. A's serif-only look is cohesive but flatter, and it has no running headers. Overall B looks more polished and more consistent.

Both share content and flaws, including a duplicated References heading. Design B has a dark cover and a serif body with gold rules, which feels more refined and bookish. Its larger chart and roomier tables read well (B3, B4). But B's first page is mostly empty, and its lead paragraphs are inconsistent in size (B2, B4). Design A is more compact, with a strong header band, running headers and a clean layout that puts the title and abstract on one page (A1). Its sans-serif text is crisp, but its pages end in large empty areas (A2, A3). Overall it is close, but A's cohesive banding, running headers and efficient flow give a slight edge.

A has a dedicated cover page, running headers and footers, a boxed abstract, sans headings against a serif body, and a navy chart and tables that look coherent (A1-A3). B is plain Times with a cramped abstract and black bars, and its table caption sits tight against the paragraph above (B1-B2). B also has a duplicated 'References' heading (B3). A has a similar duplicate, but its second heading is smaller and reads as a subheading, though it is still redundant (A4).

A uses a consistent serif system with a dark maroon band and a matching maroon chart. Its headings are aligned with the body text, so the left edge is clean (A1). B has sans headings hanging in the left margin with indented body text, which feels disjointed. B also has wide letter-spacing in justified text that creates uneven gaps (B1, B2). B's black chart clashes with the maroon band. A2's table is slightly more spacious.

B has a full-bleed cover and bold numbered headings. It also keeps the body text and image together on each page. A opens with a good green title band, but its page 2 has a big empty gap beside the paragraph and image, and thin light headings with red rules are weaker. B's page 3 has a floating image with blank space at the top, but its overall flow is steadier. A has the tighter first page and fewer pages. B's serif body text reads comfortably. The tables are essentially equal.

A packs the content into 3 pages with a strong navy title band (A1) and running header and footer bands (A2, A3). Its sans body text is consistent, and the tables and code blocks are well aligned and compact. B spends a mostly empty cover page (B1) and a nearly empty last page (B5) on little content. Its body is indented, with headings hanging out to the left, and the oversized Note callout (B2) is awkward. B's serif body is pleasant, but the layout looks looser and less cohesive.

B reads as a continuous document: numbered headings, a serif body, and content that fills pages 2-3 evenly with a cleaner set of tables. A's heavy navy bands are strong signposts, but they take up space and push a Phase 1 section break to the foot of A2, leaving a large empty gap on A2. A4 holds only three list items on an otherwise blank page. B's cover title wraps onto two lines, a small flaw. B's pagination and rhythm are tighter and more even.

A opens with a full-bleed illustrated cover and numbered bold headings that give clear hierarchy. Its serif body text pairs well with the sans headings, and its pages follow a steady rhythm. B packs the title into a header band, with light-weight headings and red rules above each section. B splits the 'Our approach' text across pages, leaving the orphaned paragraph beside the flower image on B2. Both have large empty areas at the bottom of the last pages, and both tables are similar. A's flower image sits alone on A3, which looks a bit stranded, but this is less awkward than B's split paragraph.

A keeps a consistent left margin with headings aligned to the body, and its navy header band, running header and footer give clear structure. Its chart uses a navy palette that matches the band. B indents body text while headings hang in the left margin, which looks misaligned. B also has inconsistent intro paragraph sizes (A1 vs B1), a heavy black chart, and a coral band that clashes. Both have a duplicated References heading, and A's is a small light stray one, as is B's.

A keeps the problem section together on page 1: the chart is followed by its closing paragraph, so the text is not orphaned on the next page. A's page 2 begins cleanly with a section rule and the Options heading, and it has a solid maroon running header band. B pushes the paragraph that belongs to the chart onto page 2, which breaks the flow. B's serif body with numbered headings is attractive, but its justified text produces hyphenation (uninsured, resilience), and its lighter header is weaker. The tables are nearly identical.

A has a dark cover, an elegant serif, and generous whitespace. Each section sits under a rule, and tables and code blocks stay intact within pages (A3, A4). Its weaknesses are a sparse last page with only the changelog (A5), an oversized Note callout (A2), and an awkward break in the JSON block across the page. B has clear numbered sans headings and running header and footer bands, but the JSON block splits across pages 2 and 3 (B2, B3), pages feel crowded, and the cover is plain. The heavy bands add clutter, and the italic note is small.

A uses bold numbered sans headings that give clear section hierarchy against the serif body, and has a running header and footer. B's light serif headings with rules are elegant but weaker in hierarchy, and its title band is darker with a one-line title. Charts and tables are near identical. B's text lines are longer, slightly less readable, and its rules add repetition. A also has hyphenation and justified spacing issues, but they are minor.

A has numbered headings, a navy header/footer band with running titles and page numbers, and a centered cover. Its tables and code blocks sit within one consistent text column. B misaligns its headings, which sit outdented from body text, and draws a rule above every heading, which is repetitive. B's oversized light-blue Note callout (B2) is out of scale with the body text. B also leaves large empty areas, including a near-empty last page (B5), and its footer is faint. A flows more tightly, though its code block splits across pages (A2-A3).

Design B has numbered sans-serif headings that clearly separate sections, running headers that show where the reader is, and denser pages that fill evenly with no large dead areas (B2, B3). Design A pays for its elegant serif and rule dividers with large empty spaces at the foot of pages 2 and 4 and a Phase 1 heading orphaned from Phase 2 (A2, A4). A's tables are clean, and B's tables are similar. B's justified text produces some hyphenation, but this is minor.

Design A keeps one serif family with consistent margins and aligned headings, body and rules (A2, A3). Its tables sit within the text column and its dark navy cover is restrained (A1). Design B has headings hanging left of indented body text, so the left edge is ragged. Its rules extend unevenly to the right, hyphenation breaks words such as 'safe-guards' and 'pro-gramme', and Next Steps is stranded alone on the last page (B2-B4). B's bold sans headings do give strong hierarchy, but they pair awkwardly with the serif body. A's last page is also sparse, but it holds two sections.

A has a left-aligned cover with a clear accent rule and Montserrat headings with thin rules, which give distinct section starts. Its pages hold together better: the invoice JSON stays whole on A3, and the tables sit beside their sections. Its drawbacks are the oversized Note callout on A2, the indented body text, and a nearly empty last page (A5). B has solid numbered headings and sensible running headers. However, its heavy navy header and footer bands feel boxy, the JSON block splits across pages B2 and B3, and the error-handling note is orphaned onto B4. The Note in B is also small and easy to miss.

A reads as a compact, conventional paper: bold numbered headings, a clear title block and abstract, and captioned tables and figure. Its flaw is a duplicated 'References' heading on A3. B has a striking cover page, but its section headings are light and weak, and the abstract box has awkward spacing. B's intro lead paragraph is oversized and inconsistent with the body text. Its tables and figure lack numbered captions, and the half-empty page B2 leaves a large void. B also duplicates 'References' on B4, with mismatched sizes. The cover and gold rules are attractive but add little to readability.

A opens with a full-bleed dark cover that has a restrained accent rule and a serif title, and its running header and footer are consistent. Its sections follow one coherent grid (A2, A4). B's headings are bold sans set out to the left of the indented body text, which looks misaligned. B's body paragraph splits across pages, leaving a narrow justified column beside the image with ragged gaps and hyphenation (B2, B3). B's banner cover is weaker. A's page 3 has an awkward empty area to the left of the image, but B has a similar problem on its page 2.

A pairs a geometric sans heading with a serif body, and its thin rules and indented body text give a calm, editorial hierarchy (A2, A3). B's heavy navy bands around every heading are repetitive and dominate the page. Its running header bar and sans-on-sans text are less distinctive, though clean (B2, B3). The tables are similar in both. Both leave pages 2 and 4 largely empty. A's cover title wraps over two lines but still looks fine (A1).

A's navy section bands and running header make the sections easy to find (A2, A3). Its justified text produces uneven spacing and hyphenation breaks such as 'Me-ridian' and 'pro-gramme' (A3). A also leaves page 4 almost empty (A4). B's serif type is quiet and consistent, with tidy tables and ragged-right text, but its thin-rule section headings are light and the hierarchy is weaker (B2, B3). B spreads the content more evenly, ending with a short page 4 (B4).

A's cover uses the illustration and a green band, which feels finished, while B's cover is a large empty dark field. A's bold numbered headings and green header and footer bands give a clearer hierarchy. In B the pull-quote box sits inside the image and the headings are light, which is elegant but weaker. B's repeated rules and logo add polish, but the page 3 image floats in a sparse layout in both designs. Tables are nearly identical.

B reads more cohesively. Its body text is aligned flush with the headings and left margin, and its burgundy chart matches the header band (B1). Its table has burgundy rules and tidy row spacing, and the running header and footer are more informative (B2). A indents body text relative to the headings, which looks awkward, and its black chart bars clash with the burgundy band (A1). A's justified text also has loose letterspacing, and its footer is minimal (A2). Both leave page 2 mostly empty.

A has a dark cover with a gold rule and a refined serif and gold section rules, which give it a polished identity (A1, A2). Its table and chart sit with the text on page 3 and have clear captions (A3, A4). Its flaws are a large empty area on A2 and a duplicated 'References' heading. B is a plain, compact default-looking layout with numbered headings. It also repeats 'References', and its table sits tight against the preceding text (B1, B3). B's page 3 is mostly empty. A feels more designed and easier to keep.

A has clear numbered sans headings, a running header and a steady flow, with the table and chart placed near the text that discusses them (A2, A3). B has a striking dark cover and gold rules, but its headings are small, light and unnumbered. The intro is oversized relative to the body text, and page 2 is half empty (B2). B also splits the table from its chart across pages and repeats a duplicate 'References' heading at two sizes (B4). A has the same duplicated References heading, plus a mostly empty last page.

B has a navy title band, a boxed abstract, teal rules between sections, and running headers and footers. Its charts and tables are consistent and polished. The sans-serif is clean, though the section headings are light and weak, and the abstract and references headings are duplicated or inconsistent. B also leaves a large gap on page 1 and has no table or figure numbers. A is a plain, traditional paper with numbered headings and captions. It has a duplicated 'References' heading, a table that crowds the text above it, and an empty lower half on page 3. A's design is conventional and less distinctive, while B feels more finished and easier to scan.

A fits the content onto three pages with numbered headings, a consistent left edge and a running header. Its two tables sit well under their text. B spreads the content over four pages, with a large empty gap on B2 after Phase 1 and a nearly empty last page B4 holding only Next Steps. B's body text is indented while its headings hang at the margin, and its rules are inconsistent. B's small body text is a little lighter and harder to read. The cover pages are nearly identical.

A pairs a serif body with bold numbered sans headings, so the section hierarchy is clear (A1, A2). B's light, thin headings are weaker, though its rules above them add structure (B1, B2). A splits the paragraph away from the chart onto page 2, leaving an orphan line at the top of A2. B keeps the chart and its follow-up text together on page 1, and its header band on page 2 is more cohesive. The tables are nearly identical. A's typography and hierarchy give it a slight edge.

A uses strong navy section bands with white headings and a running header bar, giving clear hierarchy and a consistent rhythm (A2, A3). The sans body and tables are clean and legible. B's rule-and-heading style is elegant but plainer. Its headings sit outdented from indented body text, so the left edge looks uneven (B2, B3). Both leave page 4 mostly empty and page 2 half empty.

B keeps the chart and its follow-on paragraph together on page 1, so page 1 is fuller and page 2 reads as a clean Options and Recommendation page. A strands one paragraph at the top of page 2 and leaves a big gap under the chart on page 1. B's sans-serif text at a slightly larger size is easy to read. B also has a running header band on page 2. A's serif text is elegant, but its dark band, small text and awkward hyphenation make it a bit less clear. Both tables are similar.

B packs content into two full pages with numbered headings, a running header and a consistent footer. Its body copy is aligned and the tables sit evenly under their headings. A leaves page 2 about a third empty after Phase 1, and page 4 holds only Next Steps and is mostly blank. A's indented body text under flush-left headings, with rules above each heading, looks fussy, and its running footer repeats the section title. Both covers are nearly identical.

A has a full-bleed illustrated cover and consistent green header and footer bands that give structure to every page. Its numbered headings and callout beside the image are clean (A1, A2). B's text sizes are inconsistent: the last paragraph on B1 is smaller than the paragraph above it, and the paragraph on B2 is squeezed into a narrow column beside a large image, leaving a gap beneath it. B's body is also indented away from its headings. A's image on page 3 floats a little awkwardly at the top, but overall A feels more polished.

A opens with a bold coloured title band and a boxed abstract, and uses sans headings with rules, so the section structure is clear (A1). Its chart carries a title and its tables are clean (A2, A3). A has odd flaws: the first page is half empty, the intro text switches sizes, and 'References' appears twice (A3). B is a plain academic default with a table split from its caption and the same duplicated 'References', plus a mostly empty last page (B2, B3). B is tidy and consistent but flat.

A has a clean cover page, numbered headings, consistent running headers and footers, and a well-integrated chart and tables with steady spacing (A2, A3). B has a bold red band and a strong cover, but the heading hierarchy is odd: headings sit at the far left while the body is indented, and the intro paragraph is larger than the following one. The Results section ends with a gap before the table on the next page, and 'References' appears twice with different styles (B3). A also repeats the 'References' heading (A4), so that flaw does not separate the two designs.

A has a dark navy cover with a gold rule and a left-aligned serif title, which feels more finished than B's plain centred white cover (A1 vs B1). Its gold rules between sections give clear rhythm, and its dense pages hold the table and chart together on A3 (A2-A4). B's numbered sans headings and running headers are clear and useful. However, B has a stray 'References' duplicate heading, an orphaned paragraph at the top of B3, and mixed chart and table placement. A has the duplicate References heading too, and large empty space on A2, which weakens it. Overall A looks more polished.

A keeps the maroon chart matched to the header band, uses a running header on page 2, and keeps the chart and its closing paragraph together on page 1. B has a hanging indent that wastes width and a black chart that clashes with the maroon. B also splits the paragraph about the loss across to page 2, and B's page 2 has more awkward hyphenation. B's bold headings are stronger, but the overall cohesion favours A.

A pairs bold geometric headings with a serif body, so the hierarchy is clearer. Its overlay quote card on the image is attractive, and its body text is larger and more readable. B's light headings are weak and its body text is smaller and cramped. B's header and footer bands add structure, but they feel heavy. The tables and the layout are about equal. Both leave a large empty space at the bottom of page 3.

Design B reads as a consistent, orderly document: numbered headings, running header and footer, navy chart and table rules that match, and body text set at a uniform size. Its weaknesses are a mostly empty cover page, a duplicated 'References' heading, and a methods sentence split across pages. Design A has a bold red title band, but its body text jumps between large and small sizes on page 1, leaving page 1 half empty. It also repeats 'References' with two competing heading styles. Its black chart is heavy, and the section rules and indents are uneven. Overall B is more cohesive and easier to read.

B is compact and cohesive: a navy title band on page 1 and running header and footer bands on pages 2 and 3. It has 3 pages with no near-empty ones. A spends a whole page on a sparse cover and leaves A5 almost empty with just the changelog. A also has awkward breaks and an oversized Note callout in a different font (A2), and code wraps mid-string (A3). A's headings are bolder, which helps hierarchy, but B's light headings are still clear. The tables are comparable and clean in both. B's body text is slightly crowded under its headings, but overall it reads as the more polished and consistent document.

Design B uses a serif body with bold sans headings, numbered sections and well-sized text that reads well. Its chart and tables are larger and sit near their text, and pages are filled consistently. Its weaknesses are a mostly empty cover page, a duplicated 'References' heading, and a numbered 'References' section. Design A has a strong navy title band (A1), but its first page is half empty and its section headings are weak, thin and light. It also repeats 'References', and its tables and chart are split awkwardly across pages (A2, A3). Page 2 of A also has a large empty gap at the bottom.

A sets bold geometric sans headings against a serif body, so section titles stand out clearly (A2, A4). B's headings are light-weight serif at nearly body size, which weakens the hierarchy (B2, B4). A's headings sit flush left while body text is indented, which looks slightly misaligned, and its Note callout is large sans. B's dark full-bleed cover is more striking (B1) and its running footer is more informative, but its thin heading weight reads less clearly. The tables are similar in both.

A packs the content into 3 pages with a navy title band, running header and footer bands, and compact sans headings; the page flow is even (A1-A3). B spends a nearly empty dark cover page (B1) and ends on a mostly blank page holding only the changelog (B5). B's Note is set as a huge serif paragraph that outweighs the section headings (B2), and its code lines wrap awkwardly (B3). A's tables have clear bold headers and a consistent structure (A2, A3). B's serif body is elegant, but its hierarchy and pacing are weaker.

B has a bold colored title band, a boxed abstract and sans-serif headings with rules, so it looks more polished (B1). A is a plain academic layout, but it is tidy and consistent, with numbered headings and captioned tables and figure (A1, A2). B has a large blank area at the bottom of page 1, indented body text against flush-left headings, unequal paragraph sizes, and a table split from its caption context (B1, B2, B3). Both duplicate the References heading (A3, B3). B's table captions are unnumbered and the Mixed logit table sits detached at the top of page 3. B's overall look is stronger, but A has steadier rhythm.

A pairs a bold serif body with strong sans headings. Section headings are clearly heavier than body text, and the intro lead paragraph adds a useful entry point (A1). Its headings hang left of the indented text column, which gives a distinct structure, though the duplicate 'References' heading is a flaw (A3). B has a duplicate 'References' heading too, with a light-weight, grey 'Introduction' and 'Discussion' that look weak next to the bold abstract labels (B1, B3). B's running header band is neat and consistent (B2, B3), but its light-weight headings are less distinct and its body text is thinner and denser. Both have a big empty gap at the bottom of page 1.

A has bold numbered section headings that give a clear hierarchy, and its tables and chart sit with the text they support (A3). Its cover page is sparse, and the 'References' heading is duplicated (A4). B's strong title band looks good (B1), but its section headings are light and weak, with a rule above each. B also duplicates 'References' with a mismatched pair of styles (B3). B has large empty areas at the bottom of B1 and B2, and the results table is separated from the chart.

A has a strong navy title band, a boxed abstract, teal rules between sections and a coloured chart with its own title, so the hierarchy is clear and it reads as a designed document (A1, A2). Its flaws are a large empty gap at the bottom of page 1, a bold abstract label that sits tight against 'Background', and a duplicated 'References' heading in light and bold, with the same duplication in B. B is a clean, conventional serif paper with numbered headings and captioned tables, but it is plainer, its black chart is flat, and the table caption crowds the paragraph above it on B1. B's page 3 also leaves large blank areas (B3).

B keeps the paragraph after the chart on page 1, so page 1 is complete and page 2 starts cleanly with Options. A splits that paragraph onto page 2 as an orphan. B's burgundy chart bars and table rules match the header band, and its running header on page 2 adds polish. A's serif body has wide letter-spacing and a hyphenated break ("resili-ence"), and its black bars clash with the burgundy band. A's bold headings are stronger and its indented body is a clean touch, but B is more cohesive overall.
